title: Prevalence of financial conflicts of interest among panel members producing clinical practice guidelines in Canada and United States: cross sectional study
authors: Neuman J, Korenstein D, Ross JS, Keyhani S
population: Members of panels of 14 US and Canadian national guidelines on hyperlipidaemia (7) or diabetes (7) published 2000 to 2010
funder: This project was not directly supported by any research funds. One author is funded by a Veterans' Administration HSR&D career development award; one is supported by the National Institute on Aging (K08 AG032886) and by the American Federation of Aging Research through the Paul B Beeson Career Development Award Program.
authorConflicts: No financial relationships with any organisations that might have an interest in the submitted work in the previous three years.
result: Five of the 14 guidelines had no accompanying declaration of conflicts of interest. Of 288 panel members, 138 (48%) declared conflicts at publication; among 73 who declared none, 8 (11%) were found to have one or more; overall 150 (52%) had conflicts, 12 undeclared. Of members declaring conflicts, 93% reported honoraria, speakers' fees, consultancy or stock ownership from manufacturers of relevant drugs. Six of 12 identified chairs had conflicts. Government-sponsored panels had fewer conflicts than others (15 of 92, 16%, against 135 of 196, 69%). Among hyperlipidaemia panels, 44 of 99 members (44%) had conflicts, and 40 of 61 (66%) in the hyperlipidaemia guidelines with declarations.
